Football.title: EFL club unveils incredible plans for major expansion including mini pitch, ‘Cruyff Court’ and classrooms
Football.content:
BRISTOL CITY have revealed grand plans to build a stunning new centre for its foundation.

The Robins confirmed that an application has been sent in for work at Filwood Playing Fields in the south of the city.





The area is around two miles away from the club’s Ashton Gate stadium with the project aiming to “create new opportunities for local people of all ages and backgrounds.”

Perennial Championship outfit City – who recently appointed veteran manager Roy Hodgson to see out the season – will base their Robins Foundation at the Sports and Education Hub.

They have promised to upgrade the outdoor space with improved grass pitches, two artificial ones, and a multi-use games area.

Concept images looking from a new car park show a modern building design with high, panelled windows.



The club’s white and red colours fade into each other on a futuristic blocky exterior.

It is said that the space will be accessible for the wider community to use.

The club also released plans for another multi-use pitch and Cruyff Court – a special five-a-side pitch – to be included.

Play areas for children have also been listed on the blueprint with an indoor sports hall and classrooms once you enter.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There will also be room for conferences, functions, and a cafe.

City add that it will have a new clubhouse for Mendip Broadwalk Football Club.

They opened their glossy High Performance Centre training ground just outside Failand in 2021 and are aiming to finally get into the Premier League.

City had looked to be promotion contenders under Gerhard Struber but he was sacked after falling down the table in 2026.

Hodgson, 78, is now tasked with steering them to safety and avoiding a late-season relegation battle.



They have never been in the Prem and are based in the biggest city in England to not host a top flight game since its rebrand in 1992.

They have now been in the Championship for 11 years, finishing between 19th and sixth.

They made the play-offs last term but have hit rocky form of late and are stranded once again.

Football.title: ‘He struggles on the pitch’ – Tuchel casts major doubt over £225,000-a-week England star’s place in World Cup squad
Football.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL has cast huge doubt over whether Phil Foden will make England’s World Cup squad.

Foden looks increasingly likely to miss out on this summer’s tournament after two unconvincing performances for the Three Lions despite starting in both the 1-1 draw with Uruguay and 1-0 loss to Japan.





The attacking midfielder has also been struggling with his form at Manchester City and asked if Foden could miss out, Tuchel said: “Well, it’s not a guarantee that he will come.

“He (Foden) tried everything. I would say he was excellent in camp but yes, he struggles to show it on the pitch.

“Obviously he didn’t have a lot of minutes for City recently. Then he came to camp with the brightest smile and was so good in training and I thought he will just surprise us and will play with the same verve and excitement but, yes, he struggles to have the full impact.”

Asked if he could take a struggling player to the World Cup, Tuchel laughed: “I can, I can – the question would be if we will.”

Foden, who is on a reported £225,000-a-week at City, was the FWA and PFA player of the year two seasons ago, but has suffered an alarming dip in form.

Although he has played 44 times for England, he has rarely been at his best for the Three Lions and has scored just four times.

Foden is competing for a place with the likes of Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, Morgan Rogers, Marcus Rashford and Eberechi Eze.

He started Friday’s clash with Uruguay as a No10 and against Japan on Tuesday, played as a false nine due to the absence of the injured Harry Kane, whose foot injury is not believed to be serious.

The Three Lions got off to a horror start at Wembley when Cole Palmer, auditioning for his World Cup spot, gave the ball away to Karou Mitoma, who started AND finished a brilliant Japan move to open the scoring. Elliot Anderson rattled the crossbar from range, before Eredivisie top scorer Ayase Ueda shook the frame of Pickford’s goal too before the first 45 minutes were up. The second half was more of the same… England were struggling to create any real chances, with the visitors hitting them on the break, their attacks coming close as they skinned home defenders for fun. Yet Foden struggled to impose himself and it looks as though he will miss out on the World Cup.

Tuchel will name his squad for the World Cup a few days before the FIFA May 30 deadline.

England will head to Florida on June 1 for a training camp and the World Cup opener is against Croatia in Dallas on June 17.

Asked if he learned anything from the two Wembley matches, Tuchel said: “I learn all the time. I learn from every training session and I learn from how the squad is together and I learn from how the players react to the gameplan and how they adapt.”

Football.title: ‘This guy, he takes off his pants’ – Premier League manager’s bizarre antics revealed by one of his former players
Football.content:
TOTTENHAM’S players have been warned that new boss Roberto De Zerbi can become so animated that he is liable to rip off his trousers!

Relegation-threatened Spurs this week put their Premier League survival hopes in the hands of the Italian, who pocketed a lucrative, five-year contract with the North Londoners.





De Zerbi by his own admission is very “passionate”, and known for his emotional outbursts on the touchline and in training.

His combustible nature has seen his stints at Brighton and Marseille, whom he left in February, cut short after failing to see eye to eye with the board.

But players who have worked with him often speak glowingly of his man-management skills, with Albion skipper Lewis Dunk praising De Zerbi for making him see football differently.

Former Portsmouth and AC Milan star Kevin-Prince Boateng played under the 46-year-old at Serie A side Sassuolo for the 2018-19 season.

It was three years before the livewire boss first came to the Premier League with Brighton.

Speaking to Rio Ferdinand for a podcast in 2023, Ghana journeyman Boateng said of Tottenham’s new manager: “He’s always 150 per cent.

“He always has fire. There’s never a day where he doesn’t want to work. Intense. He has fever.

“He’s the guy who talks the most, explains the most and he wants from you 100 per cent every day.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Don’t joke around, don’t laugh, there’s no time for that. He said we can laugh before, we can laugh afterwards, but in training there is no laughing. Concentrate on controlling the ball, of the passing, of the pace, of the positioning.

“If your positioning is 15cm off, [it will be] ‘Stop!’ This guy, he takes off his pants, he rips off shirt, he tackles you! If he sees you are a little bit tired in the morning, he’s like, ‘Are you awake?’

“He’ll pass you the ball and runs behind it and tackles you, so you have to dribble inside. He’ll say, ‘OK, he’s awake!’”

De Zerbi was in Italy on Tuesday – the day he was announced as new Spurs boss – but he travelled over to England the next day to begin his new post.

Fans are expected to hear more from their new boss on Thursday via the club’s website.



Though his first press conference is not due until the end of next week ahead of his bow at Sunderland.

Spurs are still sorting his backroom staff, though SunSport understands it will NOT include Italy legend Alessandro Nesta despite speculation to the contrary.

De Zerbi may be an explosive character, but he has been likened to Jurgen Klopp by old mucker Adam Lallana, who is certain he will keep Spurs up.

Former England star Lallana played for both De Zerbi at Brighton and Klopp at Liverpool during his glittering career.

De Zerbi has seven games to beat the drop. But he will find his new team in the relegation zone by the time his first match in charge kicks off at Sunderland on April 12 if West Ham have beaten Wolves two days prior.



Jurgen Klopp comparisons

Lallana, 37, told talkSPORT: “I always compared him with Jurgen, [because of] the passion that they both possess for the game.

“I think tactically and game model-wise, they’re completely different, but in terms of love and passion for football, they’re exactly the same.

“Definitely [he will keep Tottenham up]. Not even a doubt in my mind. Not even a doubt.

“I just think they’re very, very fortunate and I’m actually slightly jealous, I was speaking to a player at Spurs who was picking my brains about him, and I just know how they’re going to be in for a rollercoaster, but a great one.”

Lallana, who won the Champions League and Premier League with Klopp, was part of the Brighton team who reached Europe for the first and only time in their history under De Zerbi.



The Italian played an exciting style which transformed the way some of his players viewed the game – but it took a number of matches to implement.

With no time to waste for De Zerbi to save his new club, Lallana expects his old gaffer to park his plans for a tactical overhaul for now.

The former midfielder explained: “Roberto’s an extremely smart man, he’ll know that he’s not got time to play a certain way, a certain style.

“He won’t be snobbish to not understand that, he knows he’s got to go in there, motivate a group of men.

“Luckily for Roberto, he’s one of the most inspirational managers, people, there is.



“After five minutes of him speaking in our first meeting, when he joined Brighton, I was on board, I was following him, and I have no doubt that he’ll be able to emulate that at Spurs.”

Football.title: ‘Car crash’ – Invincibles star sends brutal warning to Mikel Arteta over ruthlessly axing Arsenal ace for FA Cup clash
Football.content:
MIKEL ARTETA will keep faith with Kepa Arrizabalaga for Arsenal’s FA Cup quarter-final at Southampton on Saturday.

That is according to former Gunners goalkeeper Graham Stack, who believes Arteta will resist the urge to start David Raya.





Kepa has got the nod for all of Arsenal’s domestic cup games this season – but he had a nightmare in the Carabao Cup final last time out.

The Spaniard spilled Rayan Cherki’s cross, which allowed Nico O’Reilly to score the opening goal as Manchester City ran out 2-0 winners at Wembley.

But asked if Arteta will pick Kepa again this weekend, Stack told SunSport: “I think he’ll stick with him. I think he’ll restore some confidence in him.

“I think he’ll probably have a little chat with him this week and reassure him that he is a great goalkeeper, or can be a great goalkeeper, to put it behind him and back him.



“Because I think when you get that backing from a manager after a big mistake, I think that speaks volumes about a manager. But it also gives you a massive lift as well.

“I thought it was definitely the right thing to do – Kepa was excellent in the run-up to the final. I think he deserved to play in the final.”

Stack has experience of being a No2 at Arsenal after competing with Jens Lehmann when the Gunners went the whole of the 2003-04 Prem season unbeaten.

He believes axing Kepa now could have big consequences, especially if Raya were to get injured in the game at Saints.

Stack, who was speaking on behalf of Best Betting Sites, said: “Look at this for a scenario.

“If he drops Kepa against Southampton and he plays Raya, and Raya gets injured against Southampton, Kepa has to play the rest of the season.

“What will that say about the manager? Where will Kepa’s mentality be? “Where will his frame of mind be, knowing that if his manager drops him against Southampton because he’s deemed not good enough.

“Then all of a sudden he’s relied upon and trusted to come and play week in, week out, between now and the end of the season to try and win three trophies? It would be a car crash.”

Football.title: Italy star Bastoni’s Wag suffers vile abuse and forced to turn off Instagram comments after husband’s red card
Football.content:
INTER MILAN star Alessandro Bastoni and his wife Camilla Bresciani turned off comments on social media after suffering vile abuse following Italy’s World Cup heartbreak.

The Azzurri will miss the esteemed competition for the third consecutive time after losing their play-off final against Bosnia & Herzegovina.





Bosnia defeated the Italian national team 4-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw on Tuesday in Zenica.

Genarro Gattuso’s side opened the scoring after just 15 minutes with a fine finish by Moise Kean.

But the visitors’ momentum crumbled four minutes before half-time when Bastoni, 26, was sent off with a direct red card.

The hosts put together a dangerous counter-attack with Amar Memic who drove the ball towards Italy’s area with only goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma left to beat.

But Bastoni brought him down with a tackle from behind and the referee gave him his marching orders as he deemed Memic was denied a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Bosnia ultimately got their equaliser 11 minutes before full-time with Haris Tabakovic and went on to seal their place in the 2026 World Cup with a dominant display on penalties.



According to Corriere dello Sport, however, that wasn’t the end of Bastoni’s troubles as he received abusive messages across social media.

The same happened to his wife and mother of his child Camilla and so both of them were forced to turn off comments on their pages.

Only friends and family can now post under their photos and content.

The couple have a four-year-old daughter they named Azzurra.

Bastoni will now look to bounce back at Inter, who are top of the Serie A table and chasing the Scudetto with six points separating them from second-placed AC Milan.

Football.title: Premier League icon, 40, leads wild nightclub celebrations with arm in sling after Bosnia stun Italy to reach World Cup
Football.content:
BOSNIA partied hard after their stunning penalty shootout victory over Italy to reach the World Cup.

And one ex-Premier League star led the celebrations despite having his arm in a sling.





For just the second time in their history, Bosnia have qualified for the premier football competition.

And their veteran captain Edin Dzeko was the first to celebrate.

The 40-year-old – who is also a two-time Premier League winner with Manchester City – was seen partying with team-mates on Instagram with his arm in a sling.

Dzeko was injured late in the draw and missed the shootout – but showed his leadership by battling through extra-time before being hacked down by Davide Frattesi with the last kick.



The skipper stayed down receiving treatment on his shoulder as the final whistle blew – with penalties looming.

Bosnia coach Sergej Barbarez said: “I hope that it is not a great injury to Edin Dzeko and that he will be able to be with us at the World Cup.

“Because he does not have much time.”

In the video, the Bosnian team are seen singing and dancing with a Bosnia and Herzegovina flag on the TV in the background.

Italy had battled to penalties with 10 men under Gennaro Gattuso – but it all fell apart in the shootout.

Pio Esposito blazed over and Bryan Cristante rattled the bar as both missed from the spot, handing Bosnia a famous win after a relentless barrage of chances.

Now they head into Group B alongside Canada, Qatar and Switzerland.

One fan said on Instagram: “Ironman + King + Legend = Edin Dzeko.”

Another wrote: “My goat is not sleeping today.”



Dzeko – who joined FC Schalke 04 from Fiorentina in January – has played all across Europe in the Prem, as well as in Serie A and the Bundesliga.

He’s ranked seventh in Europe’s all-time top international goalscorers with 73 goals from fewer than 150 matches.

Meanwhile, Italy crashed out of the World Cup before it began as their 12-year curse continues.

Football.title: ‘How the f*** have you got my number?’ – I approached Sir Alex Ferguson for a Man Utd trial and his response shocked me
Football.content:
A PROMISING footballer turned up at Sir Alex Ferguson’s house in search of a second chance.

Max Lonsdale wowed the former Manchester United boss with his shock decision after he was dropped from Macclesfield Town at the age of 18.





Lonsdale went from playing in the FA Youth Cup and being crowned Player of the Season to making a DVD of his best bits to hand to Fergie.

Growing up, the footballing hopeful lived only two minutes away from the United icon and his late wife Cathy.

To Sportbible, Lonsdale said: “It’s probably out of character for me, I’m not the most bold person.

“But when it comes down to it I’m willing to do that, especially when it’s your dream I suppose.”



The 18-year-old was let in but to his dismay Fergie was away on a golf trip.

Instead Cathy handed Lonsdale her husband’s number to ring tomorrow.

Lonsdale said: “The next day I rang him and explained I’d been around yesterday.

“The first thing he said was, ‘How the f**k have you got my number?!’.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Obviously I was a bit taken aback by that but after I explained it he was alright after that and said, ‘Yeah come round’.

“I drove around to his and had a good chat – he spoke to me about my football past, my injuries and said he’d watch it [the DVD] and get back to me.

“Three days later I got a call off one of the United first-team coaches to say they liked what they’d seen and [asked] would I be willing to go down for a trial.”

The bold move paid off.

The youngster had caught the eye of 13-time Premier League winner, who was so impressed by his graft that he handed him the chance of a lifetime.



Fergie had set up a two day trial that turned into six weeks and Lonsdale saw himself go up against the likes of Paul Pogba and Jesse Lingard in five reserve games.

But with United seemingly stacked with midfield options, the youngster was left empty-handed with no contract and no second chance.

From there, Fergie and United arranged for Lonsdale to head to Doncaster Rovers in search of more trials.

And when they were about to sign the contract, Lonsdale snapped his ankle ligaments and was left sidelined for an extended period.

Ipswich and Burnley came with offers after the rehab.

But when he turned 21, he retired from playing to explore the world of social media marketing instead.

Now he’s 33 with more than 400 million followers as Operations Director for Social Trinity.

Football.title: Defiant Thomas Tuchel unwavering in World Cup belief despite underwhelming send-off
Football.content:
Defiant Thomas Tuchel unwavering in World Cup belief despite underwhelming send-off

Thomas Tuchel watched his England side labour to a draw against Uruguay and a defeat by Japan but insists his belief that the Three Lions can win he World Cup is undiminished

View 2 Images England boss Thomas Tuchel

Thomas Tuchel insists he still “100 per cent believes” in his England squad even after their rude awakening. England are one of the bookies’ favourites to win the World Cup and are fourth seeds in the tournament’s tennis-style draw system.

‌



But England were brought crashing back down to earth in their final Wembley warm-up friendlies with Uruguay and Japan which raised some serious doubts.

‌



England look half the team without Harry Kane. There was no Jude Bellingham to save them. They have yet to beat a team in the top 20 under Tuchel. The draw with Uruguay was flat. The defeat to Japan was a serious wake-up call.

‌



But despite the two chastening results, Tuchel insists that his confidence in his team has not wavered. England had a 100 per cent record in qualifying without even conceding a goal.

Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition READ MORE :

Tuchel said: “I’m still believing 100 per cent. Like I said, I knew we will have a tough exam, and sometimes it is better to have a tough exam than another win and we’re not so 100 per cent sure. We will not start doubting now.

“It is difficult also for the players to come to camp, then they hear my voice for the first time, see our principles for the first time, have an offensive session, defensive session, and then go and show in Wembley. Not easy.

‌



“We will put this into perspective, but on the other side, we have built something in September, October and November, and we will rely on that.

“We opened the doors again, to see players, to give them the chance, to have a full impression and not only from the tribune.

“So to feel the players, have them in training, see what they are capable of, see what they are struggling with, and then learn from there, take the consequences, and build a team for June.”

‌



Tuchel’s split squad - naming 35 players for the two games and giving 11 of them the first week off - was designed to give them a break and also look at some fresh faces.

Everton’s James Garner impressed against Uruguay. Harry Maguire did himself a power of good. Marcus Rashford was also a big winner as he played well in the first game and came on and made a difference against Japan.

Ben White was hero and villain against Uruguay and, while he struggled against Japan, it no longer looks impossible for him to go to the World Cup.

‌



Dom Solanke and Dominic Calvert-Lewin probably feel as if they could have done more to push their claims to be Kane’s deputy. Maybe there is a slot still there for Ollie Watkins.

View 2 Images Ben White had an eventful international break (Image: Alex Davidson - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

So it was ultimately hit and miss for Tuchel’s March camp and he admitted that his biggest disappointment was not getting a winning send-off but insists they will not drop their heads.

‌



“Like I said, we will not let go of our dream, not let go of the question ‘Why not?’” said Tuchel.

“Now the most important thing is that the players reintegrate with their clubs, have a good end to the season, and then we have them in pre-camp and prepare them properly and take steps from there.”

The biggest danger now to England’s chances is surely burnout. Too many games, the demands of the Premier League which saw the likes of Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice withdraw with knocks.

‌



But Tuchel says he has a plan to ensure that the players will start the World Cup feeling fresh as he wants the pre-camp in Florida - which features friendlies against New Zealand and Costa Rica - to feel like a mini holiday with families welcomed in.

Tuchel added: “They will get a week off, the guys who are not involved in the Champions League final. And then we will go very early to the US, earlier than maybe other teams. But we will go there to prepare us for the heat and the humidity.

“But we will have an early camp also that allows us a good mix between free time and also family-friends time, and football, to arrive with excitement when the tournament starts.

“The season is a long, long season this year for the players, because some of them come from the Club World Cup, and it will not end in the end of May. It will end, hopefully, in the middle of July. And we will take this into account.”

Football.title: Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition
Football.content:
Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition

Phil Foden deputised for Harry Kane during England's defeat by Japan but his struggles in that game, and more widely, could leave him as the Three Lions' big World Cup casualty

View 2 Images Foden struggled during England's friendlies against Uruguay and Japan (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel has delivered a brutal World Cup warning to Phil Foden. Tuchel admitted Foden is “not guaranteed” a place in England’s squad because he is clearly “struggling” on the pitch.

‌



Manchester City forward Foden is in serious danger of being the biggest casualty this summer because he is out of form for club and country.

‌



Foden, 25, who has won 49 caps, started England’s final Wembley warm-up friendlies with Uruguay and Japan but was substituted before the hour mark in both games.

‌



England boss Tuchel insists that Foden was excellent in training and in camp but admitted that he failed to live up to expectations on the pitch.

Tuchel said: “He tried everything. I would say he was excellent in camp but, yeah, he struggles to show it on the pitch. Obviously he didn’t have a lot of minutes for City recently.

“Then he came to camp with the brightest smile and was so good in training and I thought he will just surprise us and will play with the same verve and excitement but, yeah, he struggles to have the full impact.”

‌



Tuchel was then asked whether he can actually take a player to the World Cup who is struggling on the pitch. “I can, I can! The question will be if we will,” admitted Tuchel.

That clearly put major doubt on Foden’s inclusion and Tuchel admitted: “Well, it’s not a guarantee that he will come.”

Foden went to Euro 2024 on the back of the season of his life but failed to deliver his best performances and since then has struggled with form and fitness.

‌



He has made 26 Premier League appearances for City this season - including five as a substitute - and managed seven goals and three assists.

View 2 Images Foden's spot on the plane is at risk (Image: Getty Images)

But Foden is no longer a guaranteed starter at City and is also facing huge competition for England as Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer are all in the mix for a place as No10. Eberechi Eze is another who could fit into that role.

‌



It looks certain that Tuchel will have to leave at least one of the big names at home this summer - and increasingly it looks like Foden is most at risk.

But Tuchel has insisted that he has taken valuable lessons from the two friendlies - even though they failed win either and lost to Japan.

Tuchel added: “I learn all the time. I learn from every training session and I learn from how the squad is together and I learn from the players react to the game plan and how they adapt.

Article continues below

“How quick they can learn and how quick they can adapt and how they can put it on the pitch. Everything is a learning.”

Football.title: Gianluigi Donnarumma speaks out with emotional statement after Italy World Cup failure
Football.content:
Gianluigi Donnarumma speaks out with emotional statement after Italy World Cup failure

Italy have missed out on a third consecutive World Cup with their players left devastated, and Gianluigi Donnarumma has opened up in a message on his social media

View 2 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma was heartbroken after Italy's failure

Gianluigi Donnarumma has confessed that he cried after missing out on another World Cup - but underlined his determination to "bring Italy back where it deserves to be". The Manchester City goalkeeper was part of another Azzurri side who failed to make the sport's biggest tournament.

‌



They were beaten by Bosnia and Herzegovina on Tuesday night after a penalty shootout. The Italians lost 4-1 with Donnarumma unable to stop a single spot kick. Italy had taken the lead early on before they went down to 10 men, with Bosnia equalising in the second-half before securing a second penalty shootout victory in less than a week.

‌



It means the Italians, who won the tournament in 2006, have missed out on the last three World Cups. Donnarumma remains one of their leading lights but, despite making his Italy debut at 16, he will now not play in a World Cup until he is at least 31.

‌



The City goalkeeper wrote on Instagram: "Last night, after the match, I cried. I cried because of the disappointment of not being able to bring Italy where it deserves to be. I cried because of the enormous sadness I'm feeling, along with the entire Azzurri team, of which I'm proud to be captain, and I know, right now, you, fans of our national team, are feeling too.

World Cup 2026 draw in full as Italy's curse continues vs Bosnia and Sweden qualify READ MORE :

"Words are of little use now, it's true. But I feel one thing strongly inside, and I want to share it with you: after such a huge disappointment, we must find the courage to turn the page, once again. And to do so requires a lot of strength, passion, and conviction. Always believe; this is the driving force behind moving forward. Because life knows how to reward those who give their all, without holding back. And this is where we must start again. Together. Once again. To bring Italy back where it deserves to be."

Italy are four-time winners of the World Cup - a total only surpassed by Brazil. However, they've failed to even compete on the global stage for several years.

‌



View 2 Images The Azzurri were beaten on penalties by Bosnia and Herzegovina

Sandwiched in between their World Cup failures was a European triumph. Donnarumma was named the Player of the Tournament as Italy claimed glory at Euro 2020, beating England in the final on penalties.

They've failed to reach those heights since with Luciano Spalletti and Gennaro Gattuso unable to enjoy similar success. The head of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) Gabriele Gravina told reporters he had asked Gattuso to stay, but he claimed that "was not important" after their qualification failure.

Article continues below

He said: "It hurts, because we needed it for us, for all of Italy and for our movement. A blow that's difficult to digest. I would have given up years of my life, money, for us to achieve our goal."

Football.title: Arne Slot confirms Alexander Isak return date as Liverpool receive huge injury boost
Football.content:
Arne Slot confirms Alexander Isak return date as Liverpool receive huge injury boost

Alexander Isak has been sidelined for more than three months after breaking his leg against Tottenham in December, but Liverpool's £125million signing is close to a return

View 2 Images Alexander Isak has been training individually (Image: PETER POWELL/AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Arne Slot has confirmed that Alexander Isak will return to team training on Thursday. Isak, 26, has been ruled out since December, having suffered a broken leg during Liverpool's 2-1 win away at Tottenham.

‌



The Sweden international missed his country's recent World Cup play-off campaign in which they qualified for this summer's tournament, while his absence has exacerbated Liverpool's injury woes. But Isak, who's recently been training individually, is close to a return and could feature in Saturday's FA Cup quarter-final away to Manchester City.

‌



"I think Alex is in a really good place because Sweden qualified for the World Cup yesterday evening and apart from that he's going to train with the group again for the first time tomorrow," Slot told club media on Wednesday.

‌



"If you've worked so hard for three, four months or something like that and then to return to team training, that's for everyone very nice. So Alex is, in that sense, in a good place.

"Of course it's only his first session, after three or four months [out], with the team but it's good to have him back because we all know who we signed and we've signed an incredible striker.

‌



"So to have him again in a team that's usually generating quite a lot chances - and maybe not immediately from the first moment that he can start - but to have him back for the last two months is, I think, very helpful for us."

Meanwhile, Slot confirmed that Jeremie Frimpong will have a scan after being subbed off just 12 minutes into his outing for the Netherlands on Tuesday. The Reds boss explained: "Jeremie, the national team doctor of the Netherlands tells us that it was precautionary that they took him out. But he will have a scan later today to see.

"Alisson will be out for a bit longer. And Federico (Chiesa) indeed came back from the national team, where he wasn't able to play. But he trained with us today, so he will train with us tomorrow again and will be available for the game on the weekend."

As for Mo Salah, the Egyptian is 'very close' to returning. Slot added: "Another example of what makes him special because the moment he got injured there was a bit of a situation where they thought, 'I don't think he's available for City.'

"But Mo looked at me and said, 'I think I will be available for City.' He just does so much for his body for such a long time that he recovers so fast. So, he will train with the team again tomorrow and if everything works well then he's available to be with us."

Football.title: Mo Salah's Liverpool pre-season act that made huge first impression on Arne Slot
Football.content:
Mo Salah's Liverpool pre-season act that made huge first impression on Arne Slot

Mohamed Salah has spent nearly two years working under Arne Slot and the Liverpool boss remembers how impressed he was when the Egyptian returned for pre-season

View 2 Images Mo Salah's fitness in pre-season left its mark on the Liverpool boss

Arne Slot admits Mohamed Salah made an immediate impression on him after he smashed Liverpool's first pre-season fitness test of the summer.

‌



The Dutchman took over from Jurgen Klopp in the summer of 2024 and had seen the Egyptian's quality from afar, but never up close. For years, Salah's dedication when it comes to fitness and recovery has been well publicised.

‌



And Slot saw that up close and personal for the first time when he took charge of pre-season, with Salah returning from the summer and coming out on top in one of their pre-season tests. For several seasons, the ex-Roma forward had been the Reds' leading light, consistently topping the scoring charts.

‌



But that didn't stop him putting in the graft and Slot was hugely impressed by the determination that Salah showed as he held himself to account.

He told the Liverpool website: "I started working with him and already the first day I was impressed by his professionalism because as with any season, it starts with a test that shows how much they did in the off-season and he beat all of them.

Arne Slot dealt fresh Liverpool injury blow as star subbed off after 13 minutes READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp opens up on special Anfield return in unique Kenny Dalglish moment READ MORE :

"He was the fittest player that came back, and I think that's the ideal situation that you want as a manager: that your star player comes back as fit as he did. He had nothing to prove, but for himself he had a lot to prove because Mo always thinks he has to prove something every three days. That hunger never stops and that is something that I find most special about him."

‌



Salah has endured a poor campaign by his high standards and will leave in the summer. Prior to this season the Egyptian has surpassed the 20-goal mark in every year he'd been at Anfield, hitting 34 last term en route to more individual accolades.

View 2 Images Mo Salah enjoyed one of his best seasons as Liverpool claimed the title in Arne Slot's first year (Image: PAUL ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

The 33-year-old's exploits over almost a decade have seen him marked out as one of the world's best players and his never ending desire to play every minute has not gone unnoticed by Slot.

Article continues below

He said: "So many good players around the world [and] he's definitely one of them in the last 10 years, that everybody talks about being one of the best there is and was in the last 10 years. To show that hunger every three days, that professionalism, that commitment to the club, to the team, to wanting to score again, always wanting to play – when you take him out three minutes before the end, he's like, 'Maybe I could have scored one extra!' – that is what stands out for me."

Football.title: Rebuilding Newcastle: Sign midfielder and striker with Sandro Tonali money and Eddie Howe decision
Football.content:
Rebuilding Newcastle: Sign midfielder and striker with Sandro Tonali money and Eddie Howe decision

It looks set to be a busy summer transfer window for Newcastle as they look to rebuild after what has been a disappointing season so far.

View 2 Images A decision over Eddie Howe's future needs to be made at Newcastle. (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire.)

It’s set to be a big summer for Newcastle United, with some clear steps needed in a rebuild at the club. The Magpies currently sit in 12th place in the Premier League table.

‌



The position is lower than they would have hoped or planned for going into the campaign, which included Champions League football. There has already been talk about possible transfer activity when the summer window opens.

‌



Midfielder Sandro Tonali seems to be at the centre of reports. The Italian continues to be linked with clubs, including Arsenal and Manchester United, as clubs make plans for the summer window.

‌



England superfan opens about selling house to fund 10th World Cup trip and early retirement READ MORE :

Lamine Yamal slams Spain fans for anti-Muslim chant with heartfelt statement READ MORE :

The club are calm over his future, with the 25-year-old having a contract that runs until 2019 with the option of a further year. However, comments from chief executive David Hopkinson have suggested that the club is open to a sale, should the price be right.

A potential sale could be central to a summer rebuild for Newcastle, as they look to climb up the Premier League table again next season. Here’s a look at what that rebuild should look like.

Spend Sandro Tonali money

Should Tonali leave in the summer, then most of the money should be reinvested back into the squad. First, the club will need to bring in a replacement for the Italian to not leave a hole in their squad.

‌



Juventus’ Khephren Thuram is one of the latest names to be linked with a possible move to St James’ Park. The Magpies have also been linked with an interest in Monaco’s Lamine Camara.

But it’s not just in midfield where the money could be reinvested, with up front one of the areas that Newcastle should again look to strengthen in the summer . After a positive start to the season, Nick Woltemade’s form has tailed off, with the German not scoring in the Premier League or Champions League since December.

View 2 Images (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Yoane Wissa has mainly been on the bench over the last few weeks. Newcastle need an out-and-out goalscorer to replace Alexander Isak.

There have been reports of interest in Tottenham’s Dominic Solanke, who could be available at a cut price if Spurs go down at the end of the season.

If there is any money left over, they could also look to bring in a new goalkeeper to the club. Aaron Ramsdale is due to return to his parent club, Southampton, in the summer. With both Mark Gillespie and John Ruddy out of contract, it will leave Nick Pope as the only senior goalkeeper option.

‌



Keep other big players

While there’s probably an acceptance that one or maybe two key players may have to be sold by Newcastle, it’s important that the club don’t go too far with the sales. As well as Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Tino Livramento and Lewis Hall are among the players said to be gaining interest from other clubs.

If Newcastle want to get back to Champions League qualification, then losing all or the majority of those players isn’t going to help them do so. The squad needs to keep the core, with the big-money sale of one or two players a year helping to supplement that.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



While it’s not ideal, it’s the reality for clubs like Newcastle, trying to break the glass ceiling. Bringing money into the club helps with Profitability and Sustainability (PSR), as well as being able to reinvest, which will be key to the rebuild.

But just as important is keeping hold of the majority of their players who have got them there in the first place.

Eddie Howe decision

One of the other big decisions that Newcastle have to make is over the future of manager Eddie Howe. The loss against Sunderland has led to questions being asked over his future.

‌



But, given that he has already led Newcastle to two Champions League finishes, he should be given the chance to be part of the rebuild.

The situation surrounding Isak and the uncertainty over his future wouldn’t have helped the build-up to the new season. If there is a clear plan this time around with the manager able to reinvest the money that is brought into the club, then he will have a better chance of success.

Changing managers in the summer would be a big risk and one that may not pay off. Howe has proven what he can do with this team.

Football.title: Barcelona's deadline to sign Marcus Rashford emerges as Man Utd stand firm
Football.content:
Barcelona's deadline to sign Marcus Rashford emerges as Man Utd stand firm

Marcus Rashford is entering the final stretch of his season-long loan at Barcelona, who have the option to sign him permanently from Manchester United for £26million

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's future is in doubt (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Barcelona have been set a deadline to decide whether they want to sign Marcus Rashford on a permanent basis. Rashford, 28, has two months left on his season-long loan at Barca, who signed him from Manchester United last summer.

‌



The two European giants negotiated an option to buy worth £26million, which chiefs at the Camp Nou are yet to make a decision on. With 10 goals and 10 assists to his name, the England international has been a useful component in Hansi Flick's attack.

‌



But according to reports, Barcelona are looking at alternatives and have asked United about extending his loan. The Red Devils, on the other hand, won't alter the deal, with ESPN reporting that the La Liga champions have until June 15 to trigger their purchase option.

‌



It's added that if Barca were to exercise that option, they could pay it in three instalments over the next three years. Rashford's entourage are said to have been in contact with Barcelona over the last few days in order to ascertain the club's stance.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Harry Maguire charged by FA for reaction to Man Utd red card against Bournemouth READ MORE :

Man Utd can give new manager £100m head start with EIGHT players set to leave this summer READ MORE :

Last month, before being re-elected as Barca president, Joan Laporta told Spanish outlet Jijantes: "We could extend the loan further, it depends on what (sporting director) Deco wants.

‌



"There are options: include part of the purchase option with United and we'll see about the rest. We're studying the deal."

But United have no intention of budging and will only entertain a permanent sale. If Barcelona refuse to pay up and another buyer can't be found, Rashford would return to Old Trafford for pre-season training after this summer's World Cup.

Should Barcelona sign Marcus Rashford permanently? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Marcus Rashford played for England during the international break (Image: Alex Davidson - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

The forward is intent on staying at Barca, though, and told Catalan newspaper Sport back in December: "It's the ultimate goal, but it's not the reason I'm training hard and giving my all. The purpose is to win. Barca is a huge, fantastic club, built to win titles."

Rashford is set to be given more minutes over the coming weeks after Raphinha suffered a hamstring injury while on international duty with Brazil. The United loanee's best period was when Raphinha was injured earlier this season, allowing Rashford to play on the left-hand side of a front three.

Article continues below

Barca's next game is away to Atletico Madrid - who they'll also face in the Champions League quarter-finals - on Saturday.

Football.title: Sinfield on panel to advise on new England rugby league head coach
Football.content:
Kevin Sinfield is among the interview panel to advise on the next England head coach to replace Shaun Wane, who stepped down in January.

Wane stepped aside after a six-year period in charge after England suffered a whitewash defeat to Australia in the Ashes on home soil last autumn.

The panel to find his replacement will consist of Sinfield, who won the 2012 Golden Boot as the world's best player, new Rugby Football League (RFL) non-executive director Sara Symington, interim RFL chief executive Abi Ekoku and RFL chair Nigel Wood, with RFL executive director of performance and participation Marc Lovering offering support.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England and Australia faced off in rugby league's Ashes for the first time in 22 years in 2025

"On the back of his incredible career with Leeds Rhinos, Kevin Sinfield represented his country on more than 40 occasions, captaining England in the 2013 World Cup, and serving as rugby director four years later when the national side reached the World Cup final in Brisbane," Wood said.

"His knowledge, expertise and input will be invaluable as we undertake this important appointment.

"As a double Olympian in cycling, Sara Symington knows all about competing on the world stage.

"She has since worked as a performance advisor for UK Sport and reached medal targets when leading high-performance programmes with Archery GB, England Netball and UK Athletics before heading British Cycling's Olympics and Paralympics programme for three years through the Paris 2024 cycle.

"Abi Ekoku has experience as Great Britain's team manager when travelling down under, including for the famous 2006 Tri-Nations win over world champions Australia in Sydney, and we are all enthused by the calibre of the candidates we'll now assess."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking before his death in 2016, the late Roger Millward remembers the 1970 Ashes Series where England beat Australia in Sydney - the last time any series was won against the Australians

The head coach role will initially be part-time to cover the World Cup, which will see England open against Tonga on October 20, with games against France and Papua New Guinea to follow.

"It is an exciting period for the sport, especially given how our athletes have already made such excellent starts to the new Super League season," Wood added.

"The autumn's Ashes series whetted the appetite for international rugby league and everyone here is looking forward to the prospect of heading to Australia at the end of this campaign for the 17th edition of the World Cup.

"We have had applications and enquiries from a wide range of world-class coaches, from both here and in the NRL.

"With the aid of our newly-assembled panel, we will now conduct interviews to narrow down our shortlist in readiness to find the ideal candidate."

Football.title: 'I'm back where I should belong' - Littler eyes fourth nightly win in Manchester
Football.content:
Luke Littler has warned his rivals he is "back where I should belong" at the top of the Premier League Darts table as he seeks a fourth nightly victory in the space of five weeks in Manchester.

Littler will take centre stage on Night Nine at the AO Arena on Thursday evening, as the Warrington ace bids to deliver the goods on home soil - live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Action from 7pm.

Following a sluggish start to the season, Littler has exploded into life over recent weeks, claiming nightly wins in Cardiff, Dublin and Berlin to surge to the top of the table.

The world No 1 is aiming to secure top spot for a third consecutive campaign, and he returns to Manchester with a two-point lead over his closest challenger Jonny Clayton.

"I've bounced back from a bad start. Back to where I think I should belong, is at the top," said the 19-year-old, who averaged 105, 108 and 106 to triumph in Berlin last Thursday.

There are eight more nights remaining before the top four players compete in next month's finals at The O2.

Littler is two points clear of Clayton, while Gerwyn Price and Michael van Gerwen occupy the remaining top four spots, and Littler knows his opponents will remain on his heels.

"Jonny's had a great start as well, but there's no doubt Jonny will keep chasing, everyone's going to keep chasing for top spot," added Littler.

"Everyone wants it, we know that. We've just got to keep going."

Littler will renew his rivalry with Gian van Veen in the quarter-finals, in a repeat of January's World Championship final at Alexandra Palace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Premier League quarter-final encounter between Littler and Van Veen

Van Veen won the pair's solitary Premier League meeting on Night One in Newcastle, with the Dutchman advancing to three of the opening four nightly finals on debut.

Littler believes he has the "fear factor" with some players terrified of playing him. The 2024 Premier League champion pointed to his sensational comeback win against Price in Dublin last month.

"I don't think I'm ever out of a game, and against Gezzy, that has shown it, from 5-0 down, going on to win," said the back-to-back world champion.

"I even said to myself on stage in my head, when I made it 5-3, 'I've got him' because he started going below the treble and he was trying to move over the oche, trying to fight for the trebles, missing doubles.

"I'm just up there doing my job and sometimes I've got that 1-0, 2-0 lead before I get on stage because that's how players think, so they're beat before they've even played me.

"I think I've said it a few times, some players, when they play me, it's their final, whether it's round one, whether it's round two, that's their cup final."

Speaking about what he needs to reach The O2, Littler added: "The last few years, I think it's been about 25 or 26 points gets you in. Call it 30 points and then I'll say I'm in."

Littler also opened up about his long-term plans after continuing his dominance in the PDC and Premier League over recent months.

"That's all down to myself whether I want it for the next 10-15 years, whether I'm financially settled and I've done everything I wanted to do," he said.

"Like Michael (van Gerwen) said, once the fire goes out of the belly that's when we pack it in."

The BetMGM Premier League season continues with Night Nine in Manchester, as Littler continues his pursuit of a fourth nightly crown against Van Veen.

Van Gerwen and Stephen Bunting go head to head in the evening's opener, Price faces Luke Humphries, while Clayton and Josh Rock lock horns in the quarter-finals for a second consecutive week.

Football.title: Brook, Bethell cautioned as Tongue escapes action over nightclub altercation
Football.content:
England white-ball captain Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell have been cautioned by the Cricket Regulator, but no further action is to be taken against Josh Tongue over a clash with a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand.

Brook was fined £30,000 by the England and Wales Cricket Board and warned about his conduct after the incident in Wellington the night before a one-day international in November, a game England lost by two wickets as they slumped to a 3-0 series defeat.

The 26-year-old had insisted he was alone but later issued a statement saying he regretted those comments and was protecting team-mates after The Telegraph reported batter Bethell and fast bowler Tongue were also present and fined for their roles.

The Cricket Regulator, the body independent from the ECB that has the power to bring disrepute charges, including fines and suspensions, if enough evidence is found, has now concluded its investigations into the incident.

A statement read: "The Cricket Regulator has now concluded its investigations into the events that took place in Wellington on the night of 31 October and 1 November 2025 prior to the third men's one-day international match against New Zealand.

Image: Jacob Bethell has also been issued a caution notice

"As a consequence of those investigations, the Regulator has issued a caution notice to Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell in relation to their conduct during that night which both players accept was in breach of regulation 3.2 of the professional conduct regulations 2025. No further action is to be taken by the Regulator in relation to Josh Tongue."

An ECB spokesperson said: "We note the decision made by the Cricket Regulator. The players involved have acknowledged and apologised for their behaviour, and the matter was dealt with through an internal ECB disciplinary process at the time."

What Brook had said about the bouncer incident "We went out for a couple of drinks beforehand and then I took it upon myself to go out for a few more and I was on my own there. "I was trying to get into a club and the bouncer just clocked me, unfortunately. "Like I said, I shouldn't have been in that situation from the start... I wasn't absolutely leathered, I'd had one too many drinks."

Brook vowed to learn from 'challenging period'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook admitted he was lucky to still be England white-ball captain after the altercation with a nightclub bouncer

Brook's statement issued following the incident read: "I accept responsibility for my actions in Wellington and acknowledge that others were present that evening.

"I regret my previous comments and my intention was to protect my team-mates from being drawn into a situation that arose as a result of my own decisions.

"I have apologised and will continue to reflect on the matter. This has been a challenging period in my career, but one from which I am learning.

"I recognise that I have more to learn regarding the off-field responsibilities that come with leadership and captaincy.

"I remain committed to developing in this area and to improving both personally and professionally."

Football.title: Staying up with the Joneses? Charlton's Nathan and Lloyd on Championship and Wales aims
Football.content:
"If they ring me up, there is not a single ounce of my being that wouldn't recommend Lloyd Jones to play for my country."

Nathan Jones has no doubts.

He would have a clear message for Wales manager Craig Bellamy and his assistant Andrew Crofts if they enquired about the suitability of his centre-back for an international call-up.

"Comfortably he's good enough," insists the Welsh Charlton boss. "Categorically, I would not think twice about recommending him."

He shares that emphatic endorsement to Sky Sports just days after Wales' World Cup dream ended with a painful play-off defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

It also comes in the context of a superb season Lloyd is enjoying in the Championship with Charlton.

The quality of his campaign is underlined by the fact Charlton supporters have voted for the towering defender to be named as the club's player of the month for the fifth month in a row.

Image: Lloyd Jones' stats in the Championship this season

The 30-year-old represented both Wales and England in youth football and qualifies for Wales through his father. "It would be a real honour to represent and play international football," he tells Sky Sports himself. But his focus right now, understandably, is on sealing Charlton's second-tier status.

The Joneses played instrumental roles in the club's ascent last season from League One and, while there have been difficult moments during this first season back at Championship level, the Addicks are well placed to establish a foothold in the division.

With seven games to play, they sit 18th in the table, nine points above the relegation zone.

"It would be a big thing for us, staying up," says Lloyd. "But I don't want to set my career up to just be staying in the league. I don't want to just take part."

Image: Charlton boss Nathan Jones has praised his namesake's performances

It is that ambition and drive that makes him an important player for his manager. Nathan first worked with Lloyd when he signed him at Luton Town in 2018. Back then, Lloyd was a young player finding his way in the game after leaving Liverpool.

When they reunited at Charlton in 2023, he was the leader Nathan needed in his backline.

"I love working with Lloyd," says Nathan. "I signed Lloyd at Luton and he wasn't the player he is today.

"The talent and the ability were there but the all-round package wasn't. Then when I came back [to work with him at Charlton] you could see a different maturity and that's just grown.

"He plays with confidence, he plays with the trust of the manager. We demand certain stuff from him and don't let him rest on his laurels. We expect big things from him and we set up for his strengths. He's been magnificent."

Lloyd helped Charlton record a club-record 23 clean sheets last season in League One. While it has been a step up this term, the 6ft 3in defender tops the Championship metrics for clearances and aerial duels won, highlighting his combative approach.

Image: Lloyd Jones wins a header - he has won more aerial duels than any player in the Championship

They are eye-catching statistics for a player getting a full-on taste of the Championship for the first time.

After Luton, there were spells in League One with Northampton Town and Cambridge United. But now Lloyd is playing the best football of his career - and he places plenty of credit for his personal development down to his current Charlton boss.

"If I need a kick up the backside, he'll give me that," laughs Lloyd when asked about his relationship with Nathan. "He's good with the way he praises me. I'd say a bit more on the tough love side, but I think he's brilliant.

"When I signed for him [at Luton] I wasn't in the same headspace as I am now.

"I went into a winning side, I didn't play as much as I wanted to. My mentality was a little bit different then, but I think this time around, I love playing for him. I know I want to do well for him.

"When I'm a bit tired out there, you sometimes do it for him as well. I think a lot of the team will feel like that. He's a big part in how my career took off in the last two or three years.

"Yes, I've always had inner confidence. I've been unlucky with injuries in my early career and also not being an absolute angel.

"But I think probably in the last four or five years, I realised what I wanted, and that's football. I love playing on a Saturday and winning three points."

It's a Friday-Monday schedule for Charlton this Easter weekend. Bristol City and Watford will have the challenge of keeping up with the Joneses.

It's a player-manager combination which has delivered dividends for both of them and Charlton too. And perhaps, in the future, for Wales…

Football.title: Dubois reacts to Harper shove: 'Now I'll knock her out in four rounds'
Football.content:
Caroline Dubois has promised to punish Terri Harper for pushing her at their first fight-week face off.

On Sunday Dubois and Harper will clash in a WBC and WBO lightweight world title unification, live on Sky Sports.

Dubois and Harper have exchanged verbal jibes throughout the build-up to the fight and on Wednesday, after facing off for cameras at Kensington's Olympia, Harper shoved her rival during a photo shoot, apparently reacting to Dubois stepping in front of her.

Harper then walked away saying: "Fool. You're a fool. What a clown… Boring."

Dubois had previously predicted she'd win their fight by a knockout in the seventh round. Now she's vowed to do it in four.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois and Terri Harper came face-to-face for the first time on fight week ahead of Sunday's huge unification bout.

"When I started camp I thought I'd stop her in six, seven," Dubois told Sky Sports. "But now I believe it'll be four."

Reflecting on Harper's shove, she added: "I was surprised, I didn't know she was on that. But it's all good. If we want to get ugly, we can get ugly. I understand that we have a fight on Sunday and we're not supposed to hurt each other now.

"So we can keep it clean, we can keep it respectful, we can keep our hands to ourselves.

"If she wants to get ugly, I can get ugly."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois trash talks Terri Harper in a fiery exchange at their press conference back in February ahead of their lightweight world title unification fight on April 5.

The WBC titlist took it as a sign that Harper is rattled. "I think she's an idiot, I really do," Dubois said.

"The game plan is the game plan. What's going to happen in the ring, is going to happen in the ring. None of this is going to affect that.

"I've always believed in myself but it's about knowing, not just believing but knowing and I know."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois vows to bring back Terri Harper's nightmares during their world title unification clash on April 5.

Dubois declared: "I don't think the aim should ever be to try and intimidate someone. I think it would be very unsuccessful.

"It's not going to happen. What you have to do is just let them know where you're at and what kind of time you're on. It's on fight time. This is fight week we're a couple of days out from the fight now and I'm on fight time, I'm letting her know what energy I'm on."

Watch Caroline Dubois vs Terri Harper live on Sky Sports on Sunday April 5

Football.content:
4m ago 14.54 EDT Tom Garry was in Munich and here is his verdict: double quotation mark Trailing 3-2 from last week’s first leg at Old Trafford, United always faced an uphill task but they gave themselves hope with one of their best performance in recent weeks, but Bayern, backed by a vibrant 25,000-strong crowd, never trailed on aggregate across the entire tie and there was an air of inevitability about their late breakthrough. Barcelona almost certainly await them in the last four, as they lead Real Madrid 6-2 on aggregate before Thursday’s second leg in Catalonia. Late double takes Bayern past Manchester United into Women’s Champions League semi-finals Read more That is all from me but fear not, the football continues. Chelsea v Arsenal kicks off at 8pm BST and you can follow along with Will Unwin. Chelsea v Arsenal: Women’s Champions League quarter-final, second leg – live Read more Share

9m ago 14.50 EDT Maya Le Tissier speaks to Disney+: double quotation mark I am fuming, to be fair. Two set pieces, it seems every game we get knocked out on set pieces. Same thing in the FA Cup. We fully beleived we could go on and win so everyone is dissapointed. Bayern upped their energy in the second half, and we didn’t match it. I don’t know why. We give all our energy to every game and this is the Champions League. Deep down we can be proud, this is our first appearance in the Champions League [proper]. We have made history. Share

12m ago 14.46 EDT The Bayern Munich players are all bouncing up and down, celebrating with their fans. Linda Dallmann has got ahold of bullhorn and is having an absolute blast. This is the team’s first semi-final in this competition since 2020-21. Share

The damage was done in the first leg with those Pernille Harder runs in behind the defence and her two goals in that 3-2 win last week.
